- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 3–5 days, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model exhibits strong lag in responding to sentiment shifts — if sentiment drops, wait 2–3 days before adjusting downward; if sentiment rises, delay adjustment until 3–5 days later.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast instead of full 30d trend.
